question: Show that $$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{17}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
explanation:
Assignment of the inverse sine angle
Let $$\theta=\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{17}\right).$$ Since the argument is positive, $\theta\in\left(0,\frac{\pi}{2}\right)$ and $\sin\theta=\frac{8}{17}$.

Determination of the cosine value
Using $\sin^2\theta+\cos^2\theta=1$, $$\cos\theta=\sqrt{1-\frac{64}{289}}=\frac{15}{17}.$$ Therefore, $$\tan\theta=\frac{8}{15}.$$

Complementary-angle relation
We have $$\tan\left(\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta\right)=\cot\theta=\frac{15}{8}.$$ As $\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta$ lies in the principal range of $\tan^{-1}x$, $$\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)=\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta.$$

Established result
Hence, $$\sin^{-1}\left(\frac{8}{17}\right)+\tan^{-1}\left(\frac{15}{8}\right)=\theta+\frac{\pi}{2}-\theta=\frac{\pi}{2}.$$
